$comment: The ONE source for the app's colour tokens. `npm run gen:tokens` writes the @theme colour block in src/global.css and src/theme/tokens.ts from this file; a jest test fails if either drifts. Values are hex. In `palette`, a shade can name another palette shade (e.g. "red-500") instead of a hex value; in `semantic`, every value names a palette colour ("gray-200", "primary" for its DEFAULT, "white"), optionally as { "ref", "note" }.

primary.$comment: Brand accent - Tailwind pink, ported from the old client.

gray.$comment: Tailwind v3 gray (pinned: v4's defaults are OKLCH and render slightly differently), plus the custom dark grays 750/840/860 carried over from the old client.

danger.$comment: Semantic status colour, tuned to read on both the light bg-gray-200 and dark bg-gray-800 surfaces. Use DEFAULT for fills / dark-mode text, 600/700 for text on light surfaces.

success.$comment: Downloaded / done indicators (same light/dark rule as danger).

semantic.$comment: Raw values for native props that need a colour string rather than a className (status bar, ActivityIndicator, TextInput placeholders, react-native-svg fills, navigation theme).

blue.note: LEGACY: the loud blue that filled chapter/file tiles. The design refresh demotes it (books/chapters distinguish by icon + subtle tint, not a filled block); screens migrate off it in later tasks. Kept until then - still referenced by existing code. Prefer the semantic tokens below for new work.

danger.note: Status colours for native props (icon fills, ActivityIndicator, svg). For text on light surfaces use the danger-600/700 classes.
